lines.text: "With force of arms we nothing can;
Full soon were we down-ridden."
For why is it that the mighty creative and guiding power of
God remains hidden from us? Why is it that we so seldom,
or not at all, experience the wondrous things God can
accomplish for us? It is simply because we wish to, and
suppose that we can, control our lives by our own initiative;
it is because we wish to live in our own strength, by our own
will, by the ingenuity of our own planning. Accordingly we
accept as real and valid that view of the world which fits into
this outlook. This view however is one in which the world
and all that happens within it appears to be controlled by
law, the sequence of cause and effect; it is the world whose
energies we master for our own purposes; the world which
we shape according to our own designs. And so long as we
see the world from this angle, it will not disclose to us the
mighty power, the guidance and government of God.
Of course there is no question that the world may be
understood and controlled in this way in so far as it is the
world of our daily work. Nevertheless the question is
whether the world understood thus is the world in its fullest
reality; whether the real world has not depths which are
concealed by just such a view; whether it has not another
aspect which we fail to perceive so long as we equate it
simply with the world of our work which, as such, stands at
our disposal. And the decisive issue for us is whether we are
prepared to be content to regard the world merely in terms
of our daily affairs, and so to regard ourselves as the masters
of the world, or whether we are going to attain the insight
that we are not in reality the masters of the world and that
in the last resort our initiative and resources are all in vain.
If we wish to become truly aware of God as Creator, and
truly to grasp His wonder-working powers; if we really
long to apprehend the one astounding miracle, an event
which makes us certain that God is our Creator, then this
means that we long to become new creatures, that we must
